segments.he: עִקַּר הַהִתְחַזְּקוּת לִתְפִלָּה עַל יְדֵי הַבֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ שֶׁל הַצַּדִּיק
segments.en: Therefore a great counsel for this is that each time, one should remind oneself of all the true and eternal goodness that Hashem has done with our ancestors and with us — with each individual person specifically. And one must accustom oneself to give thanks and praise Hashem for all the good He has done with one. Through this the heart becomes established and confident that Hashem will not withhold His kindness and goodness now either — and one's heart is strengthened to cry and beseech Hashem to save one now as well from all troubles and sufferings. As Dovid said: "Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who has led me as far as Edom?" — meaning: He who has helped me and led me until now will also bring me to the fortified city. And this is: "I will praise Hashem, praised be He" — before I even call to Him about my troubles, I praise and glorify Him for all the goodness and kindnesses He has shown me until now. For precisely through this can I call to Him. As it is written: "A thanksgiving-offering to G-d... and call upon Me in the day of trouble" [Tehillim 50:14–15] — even before one emerges from the current trouble and needs to call to Him, one must first bring a thanksgiving for the past. And then precisely: "call upon Me in the day of trouble." As our Rabbis of blessed memory taught: one must give thanks for the past and petition for the future — for when one does not give thanks for the past, it is very hard to call to Him because of the great sealing of the heart from the abundance of troubles. Therefore one must go deeply in this path — that each time before pouring out one's speech before Hashem or drawing near to any matter of holiness, one should remind oneself of the multitude of good things and kindnesses Hashem has done with one from one's earliest days until today. Through this the heart is strengthened to trust that Hashem will hear one's prayer now too — and through this one can draw close to Him and pour out one's speech before Him properly.

segments.he: וְזֶה דִּבְרֵי עֲוֹנוֹת גָּבְרוּ מֶנִּי פְּשָׁעֵינוּ אַתָּה תְּכַפְּרֵם אַשְׁרֵי תִבְחַר וּתְקָרֵב יִשְׁכּן חֲצֵרֶיךָ נִשְׂבְּעָה בְּטוּב בֵּיתֶךָ קְדוֹשׁ הֵיכָלֶךָ וְכוּ'. הַיְנוּ שֶׁהָעֲוֹנוֹת גָּבְרוּ מִמֶּנּוּ מְאד וְאֵין כּחֵנוּ אֶלָּא בַּפֶּה לְבַקֵּשׁ פְּשָׁעֵינוּ אַתָּה תְּכַפְּרֵם. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר בַּפָּסוּק הַקּוֹדֵם לָזֶה שׁוֹמֵעַ תְּפִלָּה עָדֶיךָ כָּל בָּשָׂר יָבאוּ אֲפִלּוּ גָּרוּעַ וּפָגוּם כָּמוֹנִי יָכוֹל לָבוֹא עָדֶיךָ עַל יְדֵי תְּפִלָּה. אַךְ עִקַּר הַהִתְחַזְּקוּת לָזֶה. כִּי הֲלא הַבַּעַל דָּבָר מִתְגַּבֵּר בַּחֲלוּשֵׁי כּחַ כָּאֵלּוּ לְרַשֵּׁל יָדָם וּלְהַרְחִיקָם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם גַּם מִזֶּה מִלְּהִתְפַּלֵּל וְלִצְעק תָּמִיד לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מִכָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהוּא בְּכָל זְמַן וּבְכָל מָקוֹם וְכוּ'. עַל זֶה אָמַר אַשְׁרֵי תִבְחַר וּתְקָרֵב יִשְׁכּן חֲצֵרֶיךָ נִשְׂבְּעָה בְּטוּב בֵּיתֶךָ וְכוּ' שֶׁהָעִקָּר לִזְכּוֹת לָזֶה הוּא עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת הַבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ שֶׁהֵם הַבָּתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת שֶׁל הַצַּדִּיקֵי אֱמֶת שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת מִקְדָּשׁ מְעַט כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה. כִּי אֵין מָקוֹם לִבְרחַ וְלָנוּס כִּי אִם אֶל הַבֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ לִכְלל בְּתוֹךְ הַקִּבּוּץ הַקָּדוֹשׁ שֶׁל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת הַמְקָרְבִים עַצְמָם לְהַצַּדִּיק הָאֱמֶת שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הָרַבִּי שֶׁל הַיְשִׁיבָה. (שָׁם אוֹת סו):
segments.en: And so do most of the psalms in Tehillim proceed — thanking Hashem for the past and crying out for the future. And within the words of his crying and supplication, Dovid returns to give thanks and then cries again. Go and look and you will find in many psalms that proceed on this path. And therefore his book is called Tehillim — a word of praise and thanksgiving — even though most of his words are great cries and supplications and petitions. Yet all his cries and supplications were precisely in the path of psalm and thanksgiving and praise and song and melody — in all ten forms of song. That is, as described above: in all his troubles he gave his heart to give thanks for the past — and then he was able to cry out for the future, in the aspect of: one who gives thanks for the past and petitions for the future.
